text:
sam: Heads up — planning to be in Santiago, Chile for ~90 days starting June 15. Want to confirm impact on homebase, payroll withholding, health insurance, and WFH stipend. Do I need to file anything or expect a tax nexus? Also: can we ship my ergonomic monitor there? TL;DR: what do I need to do now? :airplane:

maria: Thanks Sam — quick Qs: will you be changing your homebase? Are you intending to remain employed by US payroll or be seconded? Also will you be working Redwood hours or mostly odd hours?

sam: I'll keep homebase as CA for now, doesn't change. I'll keep same manager/timezone overlap. No secondment.

alex: If homebase stays CA and it's 90 days, typically no tax nexus for the company, but local regs can vary. For Chile, 90 days is usually fine, but we should confirm with tax. I'll ping legal and run a quick check.

payroll-bot: Automated note — for temporary cross-border stints < 183 days and no homebase change, payroll stays with US withholding. See: https://redwood.example.com/hr/temp-remote-guidelines

jordan: Regarding health insurance — US company medical plans typically don't cover routine care outside US except emergency. You should arrange travel medical or confirm with benefits team. I'll DM you vendor options. For WFH stipend: we prorate monthly. If you're gone 90 days, you'll get 3/12 of annual stipend (we prorate by full months).

sam: Okay re: stipend — is that processed automatically or do I submit an expense? I already have company monitor under equipment policy, can it be shipped internationally?

maria: Stipend: submit through Expensify with the "WFH stipend - prorated" tag and put dates in notes. Equipment: we can ship but we require customs/invoice info; you'll be responsible for any import duties and local paperwork. Please fill out this form and include the asset tag: https://redwood.example.com/hr/equipment-shipping

jordan: Also FYI, payroll withholding may still be US, but you might need to file a Chilean tax return only if you have local-sourced income — unlikely. Keep copies of travel dates and payslips. I'll flag Payroll with your temporary address dates so withholding stays correct.

alex: Legal note — if you plan any client-facing work or hiring/contractor coordination in Chile, stop and consult. Short-term individual work is fine but things escalate quickly. I'll confirm with tax team by EOD and post any red flags.

sam: Thanks all. Can someone confirm health insurance emergency coverage while in Chile? Also want to know if any payroll docs I need to sign before I go.

maria: Benefits lead @lina will confirm; @jordan will follow up with any payroll forms. Lina: can you confirm emergency coverage for Chile short-term? :pray:

lina: Short answer: company medical plan covers emergency care worldwide for short trips, but non-emergency treatment overseas is not covered. We recommend travel insurance for Chile and a provider list. I'll DM vendor contacts and a short checklist (vaccines, meds, local clinics).

payroll-bot: Reminder — log temporary address in HRIS (Homebase Change -> Temporary Address) at least 7 days before departure to trigger payroll flags.

sam: Great — I'll submit the HRIS form and expense request this week. Appreciate the quick help :raised_hands:
